Gederite
geh-DEE-rite
n. (a man of Geder or Gederah; the title of Baalhanan, keeper of David's olive and sycomore trees)
Hebrew Gederi, an inhabitant of Geder or Gederah, from gader, a wall or hedge; named once in Scripture, at 1 Chronicles 27:28.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Gederite is the title of one of David's stewards: “And over the olive trees and the sycomore trees that were in the low plains was Baalhanan the Gederite: and over the cellars of oil was Joash” (1 Chronicles 27:28). The word means a man of Geder or Gederah, towns of the Judean lowland whose name comes from the Hebrew for a wall or a hedge. The chapter is the inventory of the royal estate, and it is a remarkable passage: the kingdom of David had a named officer over every kind of property. “And over the king's treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel: and over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the castles, was Jehonathan the son of Uzziah” (1 Chronicles 27:25). Then the vineyards, the olives and sycomores, the oil cellars, the herds in Sharon, the herds in the valleys: “And over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite: and over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai” (1 Chronicles 27:29), and the flocks and the camels, until the summary: “And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagerite. All these were the rulers of the substance which was king David's” (1 Chronicles 27:31).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Gederite is a biblical gentilic and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Gederite is the name for a man of Geder or Gederah; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

It occurs once in the Authorized Version, at 1 Chronicles 27:28.

The Hebrew Gederi means an inhabitant of Geder.

The place-name comes from gader, a wall or a hedge.

It is the title of Baalhanan, steward of David's olive and sycomore trees.

Modern Corruption

Stewardship is spoken of in the abstract, where Chronicles names a particular man over the olives and another over the oil cellars.

expand to see more

1 Chronicles 27 is the most concrete chapter on stewardship in the Old Testament. Nothing in David's estate was held in general; every kind of property had a named man answerable for it, down to the oil in the cellars. A church or a household that speaks of stewardship without assigning anybody to anything has the word and not the thing. The chapter's last clause is the theology of it: these were rulers of substance which was the king's, not their own.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that a steward is a named man over a named trust, and that what he manages belongs to his lord.
